rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says that judging religion by personal analogy pairs a person with Iblis on Judgment Day, since Iblis was followed through analogy.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر فمن قاس أمر الدين برأيه قرنه الله تعالى يوم القيامة بإبليس لأنه اتبعه بالقياس

words: مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, al-Sadiq tells Abu Hanifa not to use analogy: Iblis first analogized, contrasting his fiery origin with Adam's clay.
rows.anchor: أبو حنيفة على أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فقال له يا أبا حنيفة بلغني أنك تقيس

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam Ali says Iblis was the first to disbelieve and originate disbelief; al-Tabataba'i notes that al-Ayyashi also transmits this from al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: وفي العيون عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن إبليس أول من كفر وأنشأ الكفر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: An al-Kafi hadith from al-Sadiq identifies Iblis's first manifested sin as egotism.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث أن أول معصية ظهرت الأنانية من إبليس

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq, as quoted in Tafsir al-Qummi, says arrogance was the first sin committed against God.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي عن الصادق عليه السلام الاستكبار هو أول معصية عصي الله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i explains the reported primacy of arrogance as referring back to the egotism identified in the earlier hadith.
rows.anchor: أقول قد ظهر مما تقدم من البيان أن مرجعه إلى الأنانية كما في الحديث المتقدم

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a Nahj al-Balagha sermon on Adam's creation, Ali says God charged the angels with prostrating and humbling themselves in honor of Adam; Iblis and his hosts were overcome by pride and misery.
rows.anchor: وفي النهج من خطبة له عليه السلام في صفة خلق آدم واستأدى الله سبحانه الملائكة وديعته لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says extending the prostration command to Iblis's hosts supports reading Adam as a representative of humanity rather than a uniquely targeted individual, with the story referring to creation's order.
rows.anchor: وفيها تعميم الأمر بالسجدة لجنود إبليس كما يعم نفسه

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir explains Satan's four approaches: diminish the afterlife, urge hoarding wealth from its rightful uses, corrupt religion with attractive error and doubt, and inflame pleasure and desire.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام في معنى قوله { ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم } الآية

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq swears that demons and devils beset a believer more densely than wasps cover a piece of meat.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام والذي بعث محمدا للعفاريت والأبالسة على المؤمن أكثر من الزنابير على اللحم

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida explains the name Iblis as referring to his despair of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وفي المعاني عن الرضا عليه السلام إنه سمي إبليس لأنه أبلس من رحمه الله

words: مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ
rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq's account in Tafsir al-Qummi places Adam's garden among earthly gardens because the sun and moon rose there; it presents humans as needing food, clothing, shelter, marriage, and guidance, then recounts Satan's promise of angelhood or immortality, the couple's eating and exposure, their repentance, and their descent to earth.
rows.anchor: سئل الصادق عليه السلام عن جنة آدم من جنان الدنيا كانت أم من جنان الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding verse denies that God commands indecency, this verse states God's actual command, the opposite of what was falsely ascribed to Him.
rows.anchor: لما نفت الآية السابقة أن يأمر الله سبحانه بالفحشاء وذكرت أن ذلك افتراء عليه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines qist as a just share; taking another's share is injustice, while giving it fairly is equity, so qasata means injustice and aqsata means justice.
rows.anchor: والقسط على ما ذكره الراغب هو النصيب بالعدل كالنصف والنصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to qist means keeping to the just middle in all affairs, avoiding excess and deficiency; in worship it means devoting oneself to God alone without idolatry or imitation of ancestors and leaders.
rows.anchor: فالمراد قل أمر ربي بالنصيب العدل ولزوم وسط الاعتدال في الأمور كلها وأن تجتنبوا جانبي الإفراط والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish one's faces is coordinated with the quoted command: since 'my Lord commands justice' implies 'be just,' the construction means 'be just and establish your faces.'
rows.anchor: فقوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد } معطوف ظاهرا على مقول القول لأن معنى أمر ربي بالقسط أقسطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face is what turns toward an object; establishing it means fully carrying out the act, so the command calls for wholehearted devotion in worship and exclusive orientation to God, remembering Him alone during ritual.
rows.anchor: والوجه هو ما يتوجه به إلى الشيء

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the phrase to mean facing the qibla while praying in each mosque; al-Tabataba'i rejects this historical fit because the sura is Meccan and the Kaaba was not yet the qibla.
rows.anchor: وللمفسرين في معنى قوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم } الخ

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Another exegetical reading is to face the divinely commanded direction, the Kaaba, at prayer times; al-Tabataba'i's historical objection is that the verse is Meccan and the Kaaba was not yet the qibla.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المعنى توجهوا في أوقات السجود وهي أوقات الصلاة إلى الجهة التي أمركم الله بها وهي الكعبة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A third reported reading says that whoever finds prayer underway at a mosque should pray there rather than wait to return to his own mosque; the author groups it among readings that do not fit the Meccan setting and lack multiple Muslim mosques.
rows.anchor: ومنها إذا أدركتم الصلاة في مسجد فصلوا ولا تقولوا حتى أرجع إلى مسجدي

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A further reported interpretation is to make for the mosque at every prayer for which congregational prayer has been prescribed.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المعنى اقصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة أمر فيها بالجماعة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The final reported reading is to direct one's face to God in obedience without associating anything with Him; al-Tabataba'i finds it close to his interpretation but incomplete because it repeats the following clause about sincere religion.
rows.anchor: وآخر الوجوه وإن كان قريبا مما قدمناه إلا أنه ناقص في بيان الإخلاص المستفاد من الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'a party guided and a party deserving error' is a circumstantial clause for 'you return'; the shared comparison is that people return in two parties as they began in two parties.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن يكون قوله { فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة } حالا من فاعل { تعودون } ويكون هو الوجه المشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i compares the wording with 6:94, where people come alone as God first created them; here the explicit shared feature is instead division into two groups.
rows.anchor: نظير قوله تعالى ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة الأنعام 94

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects proposed comparisons that leave the point of likeness unstated, such as being solitary at both beginnings, both creations from dust, or the resurrection and first creation sharing God's power; these readings omit the comparison and add needless ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وأما كون { فريقا هدى } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent 'beginning' is the first worldly creation of humankind, not the whole worldly life contrasted with the afterlife: the audience is humanity, so its beginning is the species' first appearance.
rows.anchor: وظاهر البدء في قوله { بدأكم } أول خلقة الإنسان الدنيوية لا مجموع الحياة الدنيوية قبال الحياة الأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects as the verse's primary sense the view that resurrection simply returns each person in the state in which he died, believer in faith and disbeliever in disbelief, because 'beginning' here concerns humanity's first creation.
rows.anchor: كما يؤول إليه قول من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, God began humanity by decreeing two groups: people guided on the straight path and people who follow Iblis and go astray; they return divided as they were first begun.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به كيفية البدء التي قصها في أول كلامه

words: فَرِيقًا هَدَىٰ وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree divides humanity between those beyond Iblis's power and those who follow him: 15:42 says Satan has no authority over God's servants except errant followers, while 22:4 says his allies are led astray.
rows.anchor: هذا صراط علي مستقيم إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

words: فَرِيقًا هَدَىٰ وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same split appears in 38:84: God swears to fill Hell with Iblis and those who follow him, then orders their descent and offers guidance in 20:123-124; following or rejecting it leads to safety or misery.
rows.anchor: قال فالحق والحق أقول لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance follows their taking Satan as ally, rather than their alliance following an independently imposed misguidance; the decree is conditional on their allegiance.
rows.anchor: وإنما قضي ضلالهم إثر اتباعهم وتوليهم لا بالعكس كما هو ظاهر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return-in-two-groups statement can explain the prior commands: act justly and sincerely so as to belong to God's guided party rather than those astray under Satan's guardianship.
rows.anchor: فأقسطوا في أعمالكم وأخلصوا لله سبحانه حتى تكونوا من الفريق الذي هدى دون الفريق الذي حق عليهم الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel is 2:148: although each person has an appointed direction, the command is still to race toward good; fixed destiny does not cancel the call to attain the happy destination through righteous action.
rows.anchor: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أينما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'as He began you, you return' may stand independently, while the surrounding context still alludes to a call to justice and sincere worship.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يكون قوله { كما بدأكم } الخ

words: لَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْبًا إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs' threat targets those who believed in Shu'ayb or intended to believe, exemplifying the threats and obstruction of God's path that Shu'ayb condemned in 7:86.
rows.anchor: هذا تهديد منهم لمن آمن بشعيب أو أراد أن يؤمن به ويكون من جملة الإيعاد والصد اللذين كان شعيب ينهى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning this threat here prepares for the later reversal: those who called Shu'ayb's followers losers are followed by the declaration that the deniers themselves were the losers.
rows.anchor: ويكون إفراد هذا بالذكر ها هنا من بين سائر أقوالهم ليكون كالتوطئة والتمهيد لما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean following Shu'ayb in the ordinary sense of walking behind someone on a road: after being told to leave or return to their old faith, the believers would emigrate with him, so the chiefs threatened them with loss for leaving their homeland.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الاتباع بمعناه الظاهر العرفي وهو اقتفاء إثر الماشي على الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the chiefs hoped Shu'ayb would depart alone: they principally hated him, while the believers were hated only because of him and for his sake.
rows.anchor: فهددوهم وخوفوهم بالخسران إن تبعوه في الخروج من أرضهم ليخرج شعيب وحده

words: لَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْبًا إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat may also be taken as directed at following Shu'ayb's religious message; on either reading it anticipates the next verse's reversal of who truly loses.
rows.anchor: وعلى أي الوجهين كان فالآية كالتوطئة والتمهيد للآية الآتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'they became in the morning' means either that they became so or that morning came upon them; its meaning was explained earlier in the parallel account of Salih's people.
rows.anchor: أصبحوا أي صاروا أو دخلوا في الصباح

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines living in a place as staying there a long time, finding it sufficient and needing no other place.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات وغني في مكان كذا إذا طال مقامه فيه مستغنيا به عن غيره بغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ka'an is the shortened form of ka'anna, lightened because it introduces a verbal clause.
rows.anchor: و { كأن } مخفف كأن خفف لدخوله الجملة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile depicts the deniers as people who had not lived long in their land: transient residents leave easily, while a rooted population is attached to kin, homes, estates, and possessions and finds departure almost impossible.
rows.anchor: فيه تشبيه حال المكذبين من قومه بمن لم يطيلوا الإقامة في أرضهم فإن أمثال هؤلاء يسهل زوالهم لعدم تعلقهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though deeply established in their land, Shu'ayb's people abandoned it and all they owned in an instant when the quake left them crouched dead in their homes; their confidence that he and his followers would be driven out was reversed.
rows.anchor: وقد ترك هؤلاء وهم أمة عريقة في الأرض دارهم وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence overturns the chiefs' boast: the punishment first leaves its victims implicit, then 7:92 names the deniers as those destroyed and truly made losers, contrary to their claim about Shu'ayb's followers.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر نزول العذاب وأبهم الذين أخذتهم الرجفة فقال { فأخذتهم الرجفة } ولم يقل فأخذت الذين كفروا الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context indicates Shu'ayb turned away only after the punishment had fallen and they had perished; his words are an admonition for later hearers.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه إنما تولى بعد نزول العذاب عليهم وهلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb asa derives from asa, grief: Shu'ayb asks how he could grieve over a disbelieving people; the remainder is plain.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فكيف آسى } الخ هو من الأسى أي كيف أحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'adhdhana means announced, and the lām in layab'athanna is an oath marker: God announced that He swore to send people over the wrongdoers to make them taste continuing punishment for the rest of the world's duration.
rows.anchor: تأذن وأذن بمعنى أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment can swiftly reach people for transgression, as in Pharaoh's people, whom 89:11-14 describes as tyrants under God's watch.
rows.anchor: معناه أن من عقابه ما يسرع إلى الناس كعقاب الطاغي لطغيانه

words: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَسَرِيعُ ٱلْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing with 'forgiving, merciful' shows God is not invariably swift to punish: He forgives and is merciful, but when deserved punishment is decreed for rebellion it follows swiftly without hindrance.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى غفور للذنوب رحيم بعباده لكنه إذا قضى لبعض عباده بالعقاب لاستيجابهم ذلك بطغيان وعتو ونحو ذلك فسرعان ما يتبعهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters say the phrase means God swiftly punishes whomever He wills to punish in this world; al-Tabataba'i says the better reading takes it together with 'forgiving, merciful.'
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا هو معنى قول بعضهم إن معنى قوله { إن ربك لسريع العقاب } سريع العقاب لمن شاء أن يعاقبه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma' says dun in 'some of them below that' is nominative as the subject, but appears accusative because it is established as an adverbial; likewise bayn in 'the bond between you is severed,' and in 'He will decide between you' it is nominative as deputy subject.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع دون في موضع الرفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means 'among them is a group below that'; the noun 'group' is omitted and its adjective stands in its place.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت كان التقدير ومنهم جماعة دون ذلك فحذف الموصوف وقامت صفته مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good and bad things with which God tested them are the blessings and afflictions of worldly life.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحسنات والسيئات نعماء الدنيا وضراءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-'arad means something without permanence, which is why worldly gain is described as a transient offering.
rows.anchor: العرض ما لا ثبات له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i understands Islam as submission to God within the ongoing order of creation on which divine legislation is founded; religion trains people to live by the laws and dispositions of their created nature.
rows.anchor: والإسلام هو التسليم لله سبحانه في سنته الجارية في تكوينه المبتنية عليها تشريعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature calls for submission to the unseen source that creates, sustains, and blesses life, and for aligning life's affairs with the real laws governing the universe; this is Islam taught by the Qur'an and other revealed scriptures.
rows.anchor: فما تقتضيه نفسية الإنسان الطبيعية من الخضوع إلى المبدأ الغيبي الذي يقوم بإيجاده وإبقائه وإسعاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reforming human life, removing fabricated superstition, and lifting imagined burdens are part of Islam's meaning itself, not optional effects that a person may accept or reject by opinion.
rows.anchor: فإصلاح شؤن الحياة الإنسانية وتخليصها من كل دخيل خرافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine religion calls people to laws and practices that serve human interests in worldly and afterlife life; it does not invent a body of teachings and then claim human interests happen to match it.
rows.anchor: الذي يدعى إليه الناس بمنطق الدين الإلهي هو الشرائع والسنن القائمة بمصالح العباد في حياتهم الدنيوية والأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the idea that religion is a set of dry traditional rules imposed through arbitrary authority, disconnected from the laws that sustain and repair human life; that picture makes worldly religious practice a burden and leaves happiness to mere habit.
rows.anchor: وإياك أن تتوهم أن الدين الإلهي مجموع أمور من معارف وشرائع جافة تقليدية لا روح لها إلا روح المجازفة بالاستبداد

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report about the transformed townspeople, Ali says he recognizes their human lineages among this community: they neither reject nor change wrongdoing, but abandon what they were commanded; God saved those who forbade evil and seized the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فقال علي عليه السلام والذي فلق الحبة وبرء النسمة إني لأعرف أنسابها من هذه الأمة لا ينكرون ولا يغيرون

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) this account of the town's punishment and says its inhabitants were a people of Thamud.
rows.anchor: ورواه العياشي في تفسيره عن أبي عبيده عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports in al-Durr al-Manthur through Ikrima from Ibn Abbas identify the people in the verse as a Jewish clan from Aylah.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس غير أن فيها أن المذكورين في الآية حي من اليهود من أهل إيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i considers it possible that the people were Arabs of Thamud who had entered Judaism because they lived near the Jewish community of Aylah.
rows.anchor: وليس من البعيد أن يكونوا قوما من عرب ثمود دخلوا في دين اليهود لقرب دارهم وجوارهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view identifies the village as Midian.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن القرية التي أشارت إليها الآية هي مدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view identifies the village as Tiberias.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي طبرية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported view identifies the village as Maqna, between Midian and Aynuna.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي قرية يقال لها مقنا

words: فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا۟ عَن مَّا نُهُوا۟ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas wept, saying those who forbade evil were saved and those who committed it perished, while he did not know what became of those who stayed silent.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية ابن عباس التي أشرنا إليها وغيرها مما روى عنه أيضا أنه كان يبكي ويقول نجى الناهون، وهلك الفاعلون

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima asked Ibn Abbas whether silent people were saved because they disliked the wrongdoing and opposed the transgressors; Ibn Abbas gave him two coarse garments, signaling approval of that argument.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عكرمة قلت لابن عباس أي جعلني الله فداك ألا ترى أنهم كرهوا ما هم عليه وخالفوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects Ikrima's inference: although the silent group disliked the forbidden fishing and did not participate, they committed a graver sin by abandoning the duty to forbid wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقد أخطأ عكرمة فإن القوم وإن كانوا كرهوا فعلهم ولم يشاركوهم في الصيد المحرم لكنهم اقترفوا معصية هي أعظم من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonishers' words show they had not despaired of the warning's effect, so the duty to enjoin right remained; once they gave up, they withdrew, whereas the silent group stayed among the transgressors.
rows.anchor: وكلامهم يدل على أن المقام لم يكن مقام اليأس
